instructions: Rinse 1 1/2 cups of the basmati rice in a fine strainer under cold water until the water runs mostly clear. Transfer it to a medium saucepan with 2 1/4 cups water and a pinch of salt. Bring it to a boil over high heat, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on for 5 minutes, then fluff it with a fork.
Meanwhile, cut the chicken into 1 inch pieces and toss it with 1/2 tsp of the salt.

Finely dice 2 of the onions. Cut the third onion into 1 inch chunks and pull the layers apart. Grate the ginger, mince the garlic and chop the tomatoes. Chop 2 tbsp of the cilantro. Slice the green chili thin and set it in a small bowl for the table.
Heat the oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat. Add the cardamom, cloves, peppercorns and cumin seeds. After about 30 seconds they will sizzle and smell toasty.
Add the diced onions and cook for 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until lightly browned.
Add the ginger and garlic and stir for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes, until they start to break down.

Add the cinnamon, turmeric, chili powder, ground cumin, ground coriander and 3/4 tsp of the garam masala. Add 3 tbsp water. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until it forms a loose paste. If it sticks, add another splash of water.
Add the chicken and stir until every piece is coated. Cook uncovered over medium heat for 6 minutes, stirring now and then.

Add 1/2 cup water and the remaining 3/4 tsp salt. Cook for 6 minutes, until the sauce is thick. You're cooking the chicken to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the biggest piece. It's done when there's no pink left and the juices run clear.
Stir in the onion chunks and the remaining 1/2 tsp garam masala. Cook for 5 minutes, until the onion chunks are soft but still have some bite.
Take the skillet off the heat. Squeeze in the juice of the lemon and stir in the chopped cilantro. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve over the rice, with the sliced green chili on the side.
method_notes: No version of this dish has 20 ratings, and none of the trusted Indian cooks has one, so this leads with End of the Fork (5 from 9): whole spices bloomed in oil, diced onions browned, a spiced tomato paste, the chicken cooked in it, then large onion pieces and garam masala added near the end. Every version also adds yogurt; here it's left out to keep the dish dairy-free, and a squeeze of lemon at the end (as Flavor Quotient and Sinfully Spicy use) brings back the tang. The page uses tinned tomatoes and a full kilo of chicken; this is scaled to 1.5 lb with fresh tomatoes and a splash of water for a real sauce. The honest time is about 45 minutes, over the 30 minute target, because the base needs 8 minutes of onions and the chicken needs its time in the sauce.
